content:
Switching from Windows to Mac, there's virtually no software limitation. Not only can all the most mainstream PC applications run on the Mac platform, but the platform also exclusively offers countless practical applications.

The one major exception is gaming. However, the latest tests show that Windows games running on Mac, whether through official or unofficial means, perform better than ever...

Apple has a dedicated game porting toolkit designed to help developers evaluate how their Windows games perform on Mac. The goal is to encourage and make it easier for developers to port games to the Mac platform.

However, as Filipe Esposito of Macworld points out, this tool is also used by players to run Windows software unofficially on Mac. He himself is one of them, and says the latest beta brings significant performance improvements, citing Grand Theft Auto V as an example.

After testing the game porting toolkit 4 beta for several days on a MacBook Pro with M4 Pro chip, I found performance improvements that fundamentally change the experience of playing demanding Windows games [...] Using the same M4 Pro MacBook Pro with 24GB of memory, the same game settings, and the same benchmark, GTA V's frame rate increased from about 106 fps under GPTK 3 to about 176 fps under GPTK 4 beta, a gain of approximately 66%. The game runs smoothly at 2K resolution with medium to high graphics settings.

He acknowledges that not every game will see such dramatic results, but he hopes these improvements will encourage game studios to consider Mac as a viable platform.
